SeasonLens — synthetic demo

Daily prices · seasonal context · currency effects

Explorer v4 · private local analysis

Analysis cutoff: 2026-10-06 ·

Historical observations, not a forecast. Futures continuation series can contain roll effects. FX reference rates are not session closes. Missing values stay missing.

Monthly average prices — last five years including this year

Five calendar years, one line per year and a black dashed period mean. Each available yearly monthly mean has equal weight. The current year uses observations only through the cutoff; its partial month is included in the period mean. Later months use available prior years. Missing values remain gaps.

Technical analysis — last 12 months

Six lines: daily price, SMA20/100/200 and Bollinger upper/lower = SMA20 ± 2 population standard deviations of the last 20 observations. The middle Bollinger line is already SMA20. Indicators use daily observations, without inserting weekends or missing sessions. Earlier history warms up indicators before the displayed 12 calendar months; a full window is required. FX panels use reference observations. The Y-axis fits visible lines; CSV exports all cutoff-visible observations and indicators.

Monthly changes

Change in the last observed price versus the previous calendar month's last observed price. Green: positive; purple: negative; white: zero; gray: missing. * Current month is partial. Missing previous calendar months produce missing returns. No roll adjustment is applied.

Same partial-month comparison

For the cutoff month, compare each preceding year's observations only through the same calendar day. February 29 is clamped to February 28 in non-leap years. Years receive equal weight; observed counts can differ.

Seasonal levels in original display units

Full historical calendar-month means. The current cutoff month may be partial; use the matched comparison above for that month.

Normalized seasonal comparison

Each year's first observed positive daily value is indexed to 100. Charts summarize monthly mean index levels, then give each available year equal weight. The first observation can occur after January; inspect coverage. This is a continuation-price index, not an investable total return.

Import a local CSV

The local app processes the selected CSV on your computer. This panel imports one explicitly selected series into the private database; it does not contact a market-data provider.

SeasonLens · all figures calculated locally · restricted inputs and embedded observations remain private. Counts do not certify complete trading sessions. Calendar age is measured against the analysis cutoff, not your computer's current date. Missing calendar months are counted from the first visible observation month through the cutoff month.
